title: Missed Sessions at the Snowsports School and the Basis for Raising a School Fee
content:
A participant who does not present at the meeting point within the product's grace period has missed the session, and the booking is marked as missed rather than cancelled.

## When the missed session fee is raised

The missed session fee is raised only once the assessment lag has run out counted in calendar days from the day the session was due to run.

Calendar days are counted forward from the anchor date, the anchor date itself counting as day zero, every day of the week counting alike, and a calendar day is never mixed with a full 24-hour period; where the resulting boundary falls on a date that does not exist in the target month, the last day of that month is used. The day the session was due to run is read from the booking record, matched by the booking reference. The fee falls due on the day the lag runs out and on every day after it.

## What the fee is

The fee is the product's missed session share of the booking price, and it is raised once for the booking however many sessions of a block were missed together.

## Against what a fee may be raised

A fee is raised against a booking only while the booking record stands in the firm, under-way, cancelled or missed state. In the asked-for, waiting, delivered and closed states no fee is raised. The clause governs every school fee raised against a booking, whatever the fee is for — a late cancellation, a missed session, a move to another date, a re-registration or a named instructor.

## What a missed session does not carry

A missed session is never made up: the makeup allowance covers sessions the household gave notice of, not sessions nobody turned up for.

## Where the participant was prevented

Where the participant was prevented from presenting by the mountain being closed or by the instructor not arriving, no fee is raised at all and the session is treated as lost to the mountain.

## Boundary readings of the assessment lag

Take a product whose assessment lag is 2 calendar days and a session that was due to run on the eighteenth of a month. Counting the eighteenth as day zero, the nineteenth is day one and the twentieth is day two, so the lag has run out on the twentieth.

| Day the fee is considered | Reading |
| --- | --- |
| the nineteenth | the lag has not run out; the fee is not yet raised |
| the twentieth | the lag has run out on that day; the fee may be raised |
| the twenty-first | the lag has run out; the fee may be raised |

The grace periods, missed session shares, assessment lags, late cancellation shares, move fees, re-registration fees and named-instructor fees this basis turns on are published product by product on the Snowsports School tariff.
